## Overview
- 3,000 bp, clean ACGT sequence, 52.1% GC (no ambiguous bases), no large GC drift (windows range 46–58% GC).
- **The region is dominated by a single, complete bacterial protein-coding gene.** Apart from that, the sequence is unremarkable.

## 1. The main feature: a complete protein-coding gene at nt 158–2854

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Strand / frame | + strand, reading frame 2 (codons at nt 158, 161, 164…) |
| Start codon | ATG at nt **158–160** |
| Stop codon | TAA at nt **2852–2854** |
| Length | 2,697 nt = 899 codons incl. stop → **898 aa protein** |
| Ribosome binding site | **GGAGGG** at nt **145–150**, 7-nt spacer (nt 151–157) → canonical Shine-Dalgarno |

Why this is unambiguously a real gene rather than a chance open frame:
- **Zero in-frame stop codons over 899 codons.** Random DNA of this composition would contain ~39. Every other frame in the region shows a normal stop density (e.g. 51 stops in +1, 59 in +3, 51 in –2).
- Real codon bias, not composition noise: G at wobble positions 36.6% (pos-3 GC = 59.4%), G 33.8% at pos-1, and CTG alone accounts for 58/899 codons (54% of all Leu). Flanking intergenic DNA (nt 1–157, 2855–3000) shows none of this bias and has normal stop-codon density.

## 2. The product: a hydrophobic, 898-aa protein of unknown function
- Distinctly hydrophobic composition: 48% hydrophobic residues; **L+A+V+I alone = 36%** (Leu 108 = 12%); mean Kyte-Doolittle hydropathy +0.16 (positive).
- Putative **membrane-associated**, distributed hydrophobic segments (peak 19-aa-window hydropathy): aa **100–142** (2.24), **280–342** (2.54), **701–740** (2.06), **763–796** (1.91), **825–892** (2.28). The C-terminal third (aa ~700–898) is the most hydrophobic part of the protein.
- Only one textbook transmembrane helix is present: an uninterrupted, completely uncharged 17-aa run **LFAAGVIALMVAISTLL** at aa **118–134** (nt 509–557, mean KD 2.51). The other hydrophobic stretches are broken by occasional charged residues, so they are amphipathic rather than simple TM helices.
- **No N-terminal signal peptide** (hydropathy of aa 1–25 is negative), so this is not a secreted/lipoprotein precursor.
- **No recognizable functional motif** after a broad scan: no Walker-A/P-loop NTPase, no HExxH metalloprotease, no GxSxG lipase/esterase, no Rossmann GGxG, no DEAD/DEAH, no aaRS HIGH/KMSKS, no PD-(D/E)xK nuclease, no Cys-cluster metal site (Cys at aa 42, 96, 236, 240, 371, 467, 478, 580, 785, 832), no LPXTG, RGD, coiled-coil heptad or leucine-zipper repeat, and no internal repeats above 4 aa. → **a hypothetical/conserved-unknown membrane protein.**

## 3. Things I checked and found NOT notable
- **No repeats:** no exact repeated word longer than **11 bp** anywhere in 3,000 bp (11-mers at nt 1362/1687, 1452/2721, 2550/2595); longest homopolymer is only 6 nt (nt 1470, 2181) → **no CRISPR array, no tandem/vNTR repeats, no low-complexity tracts.**
- **No mobile-element signature:** no inverted or direct repeats shared between the two ends of the region, no flanking duplicated target sites.
- **No regulatory structures:** no perfect palindrome ≥14 bp; only small hairpins (largest stems 6–7 bp at nt 913, 1604, 1981, 2831); no convincing -35/-10 promoter pair upstream and **no rho-independent terminator** (stem-loop + U-tract) downstream of the stop codon.
- **No tRNA/rRNA-like structure** and no obvious DNA-uptake/attC/USS motifs.
- The only other sizeable ORF is a 173-codon antisense ORF at nt **1735–2256** on the reverse strand, entirely contained inside the main gene → almost certainly spurious.
- The flanks (nt 1–157 and 2855–3000, GC ~47–50%) are plain intergenic DNA.

## Bottom line
The region contains essentially one thing of interest: a complete, well-constituted bacterial gene spanning nt 158–2854 (+ strand, frame 2) with a textbook Shine-Dalgarno site at nt 145–150. Its 898-aa product is unusually hydrophobic (48% hydrophobic residues, 36% L+A+V+I) with one clear TM helix at aa 118–134 and additional amphipathic hydrophobic regions at aa 100–142, 280–342, 701–740, 763–796 and 825–892, so it is most likely an integral or membrane-associated protein — but it carries no identifiable motif or domain signature, so its function cannot be assigned from sequence alone.

**Recommended next step:** run the 898-aa translation (and the nt 158–2854 nucleotide sequence) through BLASTP/BLASTX and HMMER against Pfam — this analysis was done offline, so no database search was possible here.
